name: cloudflare
summary: Put the store's rate limits, geo blocks, custom rules, managed rulesets and origin lock on its Cloudflare zone.

env.name: CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID
env.comment: The zone's ID (Cloudflare dashboard, the domain's Overview page, API section)

env.name: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN
env.comment: An API token scoped to that zone only, with Zone › Zone › Read, Zone › Zone WAF › Edit, Zone › Cache Rules › Edit and Zone › Transform Rules › Edit

next: Create the API token in the Cloudflare dashboard (My Profile, API Tokens) with four permissions on this zone only: Zone › Zone › Read, Zone › Zone WAF › Edit, Zone › Cache Rules › Edit and Zone › Transform Rules › Edit.

Point your domain through Cloudflare and set NYMBAL_PUBLIC_URL in .env to it. The first nymbal security:apply creates NYMBAL_ORIGIN_SECRET in .env and a rule that sends it from Cloudflare; then set NYMBAL_ORIGIN_SECRET on your host (apply prints the command) and restart, so the API answers only requests that crossed Cloudflare and reads each shopper's address from CF-Connecting-IP on them. Leave NYMBAL_CLIENT_IP_HEADER unset (a header of your own replaces Cloudflare's and counts without the secret), and keep NYMBAL_TRUSTED_PROXIES to your platform's proxy, never Cloudflare's ranges.

The zone's plan limits security.rateLimit: the Free plan allows one rate limit with a 10s window, Pro two with 10s or 1m (the scaffold's four fit Business and up). A throttle action needs the Enterprise plan: on Free, Pro or Business change the scaffold's two throttle entries (/api/*, /webhooks/*) to block or challenge. nymbal security:plan names each limit the plan refuses.
Run nymbal security:plan to see the rules, then nymbal security:apply to put them on the zone; nymbal security:drift reports a dashboard edit.
